correctness.rationale: The proof constructs a unique group phase for every useful state by common accepting continuations, forces a distinct underlying simple graph edge above each of the k*2^(k-1) Boolean-cube edges, and uses E<=4(N-1)/3 for connected bipartite cacti to obtain N>=1+3k*2^(k-3). A 2^k fooling set and a parity DFA independently give exact unrestricted NFA state complexity. Critical quantifiers, connectedness, epsilon-free assumption, and trimming are proved; checker.py replay independently corroborated 12 cube dimensions, 3,500 bipartite cacti, and 97,742 word tests. Finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The independent even-count language is a canonical finite-group kernel with exact ordinary NFA size 2^k; proving cactus NFA size at least (3k/8+2^(-k)) times larger gives a nonconstant size penalty for a natural structural representation constraint highlighted by a recent existence theorem. The proof supplies a reusable phase-label/forced-Cayley-edge plus sparse-graph method, while avoiding any unsupported sharpness or fixed-alphabet claims.
